content.tldr: The Iceberg catalog tracks the current metadata pointer for every table and enforces atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) commits across concurrent transactions.
content.simple_explanation: Because an Iceberg table's state is encapsulated in an immutable root metadata file (`vN.metadata.json`), engines need a centralized registry that points to the current active metadata version. The Catalog acts as this central source of truth. Common catalog implementations include: REST Catalog (the vendor-neutral industry standard protocol used by Polaris and Unity), AWS Glue Catalog, Hive Metastore, JDBC (Postgres/MySQL), and Nessie (offering Git-like branching for data lakes).
content.real_world_example: The domain registrar for the internet: when you look up a website name, the central DNS registry points to the active IP address; when servers migrate, updating the registrar redirects all global visitors instantly.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: The Iceberg REST Catalog protocol prevents vendor lock-in, enabling seamless interoperability between Snowflake, Databricks, Trino, and Spark on the exact same underlying storage bucket.
